land.text: the Moldavian SSR, created in 1940, which 'declared independence and took the name Moldova' on 27 August 1991

predecessors.note: The left bank of the Dniester (Transnistria) was already 'under the de facto control of the breakaway government of Transnistria since 1990' (Moldova page), so the Republic governs the right bank only.

correction.text: the Republic of Moldova in the year of its declaration of independence (27 August 1991), the land its government held: the same outline as Cliopatria's 1992 shape, only the years change

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Moldova in 1992 but the page dates the declaration to 27 August 1991 ('the Moldavian SSR declared independence and took the name Moldova'). The shape already leaves out the left bank, which had been under Transnistrian de facto control since 1990.

1992-2023, 27,293 km2 against the infobox 33,843 km2 (ratio 0.81). The shape leaves out the gazetteer's Transnistria (12 cells; the War page says Transnistria is 'slightly more than one tenth of Moldova's territory') and the four cells of Bender district, i.e. Moldova as governed after the 21 July 1992 ceasefire; the remaining gap is the coarse outline (45 vertices). Accepted as de facto control; the claim to the left bank is carried by the ledger's contest events.

2024, identical to the 1992 shape. The Moldova page records no border change after 1992 beyond a swap with Ukraine ('in 1999 Moldova acquired from Ukraine (in exchange for ceding a stretch of contested road in the east of the country)'), too small to draw (a '0.45 kilometer river frontage to the Danube'); the page dates it to 1999 (reviewer eu-22-f; the draft said undated).

region.text: the right bank of the Dniester, the part of the Moldavian SSR that the new government held; the left bank was under Transnistrian de facto control

ledger.note: 1991, 27 August: Moldova declares independence. 'On 27 August 1991, as the ... Moldavian SSR declared independence and took the name Moldova.' The page gives no boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1992 shape, which excludes Transnistria.

region.text: the left bank of the Dniester and the Bender (Tighina) bridgehead on the right bank

ledger.note: 1992, March: the Transnistria War's main phase begins. 'Fighting intensified on 1 March 1992'; the infobox gives the main phase as 2 March to 21 July 1992 (the conflict itself 'broke out on 2 November 1990 in Dubasari', before the Republic existed).

region.text: the left bank of the Dniester and Bender

ledger.note: 1992, 21 July: the ceasefire. 'A ceasefire agreement was signed on 21 July' (Yeltsin and Snegur); it provided for 'five Russian battalions, three Moldovan battalions and two PMR battalions' under the Joint Control Commission. Result: 'Russo-Transnistrian victory'.

region.text: Bender (Tighina) on the right bank, where 'parts of the city of Bender, including the center, were retaken by PMR forces' in June 1992; the left bank had been under the breakaway government's de facto control 'since 1990', before the Republic existed

ledger.note: 1992: Bender is lost de facto. The War page: 'In the course of the following days, parts of the city of Bender, including the center, were retaken by PMR forces'; the ceasefire of 21 July froze the line. Transnistria 'becomes a de facto independent state, but remains internationally recognized as part of Moldova'. The left bank itself is not part of this loss: the Moldova page says it has been under the breakaway government's de facto control 'since 1990', and this dossier's found region (Cliopatria's 1992 shape) already leaves it out. Reviewer eu-22-f narrowed the region from Transnistria plus Bender to Bender, matching the transnistria dossier's 1992 gain of Bender. The War page does not say who holds all of Bender; the region follows Cliopatria's shape, which leaves Bender out.

wars.name: Transnistria War

zones.text: the left bank of the Dniester and Bender

wars.outcome: Russo-Transnistrian victory: ceasefire of 21 July 1992 left Transnistria a de facto independent state, recognised internationally as part of Moldova, with a mixed peacekeeping force.
wars.note: Infobox '2 November 1990 - 21 July 1992', main phase 2 March to 21 July 1992; Battle of Bender 19-21 June 1992 ('the 14th Army intervening to drive out the Moldovan army'). Moldova's founding (August 1991) falls inside the war, so the ledger's contest starts at the 1992 main phase.

certainty.note: The Prut (the Romanian frontier) and the former republican border with Ukraine are sharp; the Transnistrian line is a ceasefire line of 21 July 1992 and stays soft, and Gagauzia is an autonomous unit inside the state, not a border.

sources.title: Moldova

sources.title: Transnistria War

notes: Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Cliopatria's Moldova shape is the government-held right bank without Transnistria and Bender, so no correction beyond the 1991 start. The Moldova page was silent on: the 1994 autonomy of Gagauzia, the 1991-92 status of Bender city (the War page says only that the PMR retook parts including the centre), and the name change: the page ties it to 27 August 1991 while the existing moldavian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier (another batch, another page) dates the rename to 23 May 1991. Transnistria: dossier transnistria exists (batch eu-22-x); Cliopatria's 'Russian-occupied territories' row (1992-2024, 7,000 km2, bbox 28.3-44.5 E) overlaps Moldova in the gazetteer, so the transnistria and russian-occupied-territories dossiers should settle whether the left bank is drawn as a state or as occupied land. No ruler list opened. All region names resolve (Transnistria, Bender); nothing needed from the gazetteer. Reviewer eu-22-f: the Moldova page does date the Moldova-Ukraine land exchange ('in 1999 Moldova acquired from Ukraine ... a 0.45 kilometer river frontage to the Danube'), too small to draw.
